answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each new identity pay a verifiable, non-transferable entry cost at a single jetty: to join, an agent must complete a timed proof-of-work puzzle tied to its public key and lock a small bond that is slashed if it is caught voting twice. Like crossing a tundra, creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive in time and capital, while honest agents pay once. Established members attest newcomers on an island of trust, so fakes cannot gain voting power without costly endorsements that punish sponsors.
